question: What international conference formally established the modern concept of Primary Health Care in 1978?
explanation: The Alma-Ata Declaration of 1978 set the global agenda for primary health care as the key to achieving health for all. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why did the focus of health care shift toward primary health care after 1978?

options.A: To move away from costly hospital-focused care toward prevention
options.B: To stop funding urban teaching hospitals completely
options.C: To make all specialized surgeries available in rural health posts
options.D: To replace traditional healers with trained doctors in villages

explanation: Primary health care was introduced to prioritize community wellness and prevention rather than relying solely on expensive curative hospital treatments. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h1)

question: What does equitable distribution mean in primary health care?

options.A: Patients must pay equal amounts of money for all drugs
options.B: Every village must have a fully equipped general hospital
options.C: Doctors and nurses must rotate through rural areas yearly
options.D: Health services are shared fairly regardless of social status

explanation: Equitable distribution ensures that care reaches everyone based on need rather than ability to pay or social standing. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h2)

question: A community health nurse distributes scarce mosquito nets to pregnant mothers and infants first. Which principle is applied here?
explanation: Prioritizing vulnerable groups like pregnant mothers and infants ensures fair distribution of limited resources to those most at risk. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why is community participation essential for the success of health programs?

options.A: It ensures local ownership and long-term sustainability
options.B: It eliminates the need for professional health workers
options.C: It prevents the community from asking for modern drugs
options.D: It reduces the salaries that government pays to nurses

explanation: When communities help plan and run their own health programs, they maintain and support them long after external funding ends. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which group acts as a primary link between rural households and the formal health system?

options.A: Federal ministers of health and finance
options.C: Village health committees and local volunteers

explanation: Local volunteers and health committees mobilize the community and connect residents to primary health clinics. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of intersectoral collaboration in health care?

options.A: To address the social and environmental roots of illness
options.B: To increase taxes collected from commercial businesses
options.C: To transfer all health ministry duties to agriculture
options.D: To reduce the number of hospitals built by the government

explanation: Health depends on factors like food, clean water, and education, requiring teamwork across different sectors outside medicine. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: A clinic nurse partners with local agriculture officers to teach mothers about growing protein-rich crops. What strategy is this?
explanation: Working with agriculture to improve nutrition demonstrates collaboration between different sectors to promote community health. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is a key requirement of appropriate technology in health care?

options.A: It must be imported directly from industrialized nations
options.B: It must rely entirely on computerized digital systems
options.C: It must be affordable and maintainable locally
options.D: It must be restricted to large urban teaching hospitals

explanation: Appropriate technology uses methods and tools that the local community can afford, understand, and repair themselves. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why are solar-powered refrigerators considered appropriate technology for rural clinics?

options.A: They freeze vaccines much faster than electric freezers
options.B: They cost nothing to purchase from international donors
options.C: They overcome unreliable electricity grids using local sunlight
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for trained vaccine handlers

explanation: Solar power relies on abundant local sunlight, making it practical where electricity supply is unstable or absent. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which service is officially recognized as a core component of primary health care?
explanation: Childhood immunization is one of the core, non-negotiable components of essential primary health care services. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is the provision of safe water and basic sanitation included in primary health care?

options.A: Unclean water and poor sanitation are major causes of preventable infectious diseases
options.B: The government makes more revenue from water rates than from drug sales
options.C: Sanitation control is the only way to treat chronic non-communicable diseases
options.D: Water engineers are required to work inside primary health clinics daily

explanation: Waterborne and sanitation-related illnesses cause a high burden of disease, making clean water fundamental to health. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h6)

question: A community health nurse in a rural Nigerian village organizes mothers into a cooperative to fund emergency transport to the clinic. Which nursing role does this reflect?
explanation: Organizing local women to solve transport barriers builds community self-reliance and empowerment in health care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is a common operational challenge faced by primary health care nurses in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of advanced surgical equipment in clinics
options.B: Complete lack of patients seeking care at primary centers
options.C: Shortages of staff and underfunded facilities in rural areas
options.D: Too many doctors competing with nurses for community outreach

explanation: Primary health facilities in many rural areas struggle with poor funding, infrastructure deficits, and staffing shortages. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h7)
